spec_contract.notes: The batch expresses one coherent outcome: upgrade from open-loop reasoning to an honest scored closed-loop proof. Dependencies and claim boundaries are explicit.

implementation_plan.notes: The sequence is approval-ready: contract/scorer, local runner, inference bridge, then live proof. Runtime blockers are separated from locally testable work.

evidence_quality.notes: The plan requires traceable observe-infer-act-observe evidence and records the missing metadata checker. Final evidence quality depends on TASK-160 live artifacts.

claim_honesty.notes: The plan explicitly separates cached replay, paused receding-horizon control, and real-time control, and preserves real_time_vla_control=false unless cadence proof exists.

implementation_path.notes: The ticket sequence is ordered correctly: score contract, local runner, inference bridge, then live Kasm proof. TASK-158 should keep live CARLA changes behind adapter seams to avoid destabilizing existing demo-video code.

evidence_quality.notes: The proposed ClosedLoopRunTrace gives judge-visible proof of observe/infer/act/observe recurrence. TASK-160 still depends on remote Kasm availability and should record blockers instead of upgrading claims if live execution fails.

deadline_roi.notes: Paused closed-loop proof is the highest ROI path to a stronger SoTA submission because it upgrades the core autonomy claim without chasing unrealistic real-time Alpamayo latency.

findings.title: Keep closed-loop scorer strict about post-action observations
findings.detail: TASK-157 implementation should reject traces where a later model input does not have a frame id or timestamp after the previous applied control chunk. This is the main guard against relabeling cached/open-loop evidence.

findings.title: Treat real-time mode as out of scope until latency proof exists
findings.detail: The current Alpamayo latency makes real-time closed-loop control implausible. TASK-157 should score real_time claims as invalid unless tick cadence and end-to-end inference latency are both present and below the configured budget.

findings.title: Use the simplest live blocker case first
findings.detail: TASK-160 should prefer a clean static-blocker stop or slow-down case before compound detours. A short causal stop is more persuasive than a complex route that risks lane or control artifacts.
